candidates.explanation: After verifying the reset hash and updating the user's password (user.password = password; usersService.update), the method never invalidates the user's existing sessions (e.g. via sessionService.deleteByUserId). Existing refresh tokens/sessions stay valid, so devices already signed in can still call refreshToken and renew their login after a password reset.

Refresh only checks that the session exists by hash and that the user has a role; it has no check tying the session to the current password state, so sessions created before a password reset continue to renew.

fix.description: In AuthService.resetPassword, after usersService.update(user.id, user), delete all sessions for that user (e.g. await this.sessionService.deleteByUserId({ userId: user.id })) so every device's refresh token is revoked and must sign in again.
